name: Spiritual left
summary: The spiritual left grounds left-wing goals of peace, economic justice and ecological care in religious or spiritual traditions rather than secular ones. It holds that politics should be judged by love, generosity and awe rather than money and power alone, and it contests the religious right's claim to speak for faith. Its best-known voices are Rabbi Michael Lerner of Tikkun and Jim Wallis of Sojourners.
scope: The contemporary American religious and spiritual progressive current represented by Michael Lerner (Tikkun, the Network of Spiritual Progressives, the New Bottom Line and Spiritual Covenant) and Jim Wallis (Sojourners, God's Politics). It is interfaith and mostly liberal-democratic in method. It excludes secular left, theocratic and conservative religious politics, and many specific policy questions are unaddressed by these writers, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.author: Michael Lerner
sources.usedFor: The New Bottom Line, Global Marshall Plan, opposition to the Iraq war, two-state position and opposition to imposing a religion.

sources.title: Interview with Rabbi Michael Lerner
sources.author: Grist
sources.usedFor: Ecology as a spiritual movement, consuming less, universal health care, opposing cuts to programs for the poor.

sources.title: Love Thine Political Enemies: Reflections on God's Politics and the Teachings of Christ

sources.usedFor: Wallis on poverty, budgets as moral documents, war, church and state, and faith in civil rights.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Lerner explicitly backs universal health care and adequate education for all as part of a higher standard of living.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the poverty-first stance that wages should support dignified living.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lerner wants institutions judged by a New Bottom Line of love and caring rather than money and efficiency, and rejects a globalization of selfishness.

public-ownership.rationale: Lerner backs economic democracy, but neither source names public ownership of utilities; inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Lerner attacks the religious right for cutting taxes for the rich while cutting programs for the poor.

unions-good.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the economic democracy and social justice commitments.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: the New Bottom Line subordinates property and profit to caring, though no source discusses property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Lerner's covenant would add a social responsibility requirement to corporate conduct and judge firms by the New Bottom Line.

cut-welfare.rationale: Lerner condemns cuts to social programs for the poor as a misuse of religion.

worker-ownership.rationale: Economic democracy points toward worker control, but the sources do not specify worker ownership; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of a Strategy of Domination and security-first politics; not discussed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source addresses drug policy and adherents are likely split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the love-and-caring ethos pulls one way and civil liberties the other.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on grassroots spiritual movement-building over top-down rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Lerner wants government to fund health, education and anti-poverty programs, so he does not view the state as harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the commitment to peace and a Strategy of Generosity.

empower-police-military.rationale: Lerner rejects militarism and the Strategy of Domination and wants resources redirected to a Global Marshall Plan.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; religious and feminist strands of the spiritual left disagree.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses both local community and national and global programs.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on caring and kindness; no source discusses prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Wallis stresses family but liberal spiritual progressives reject the religious right's family politics; adherents are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not stated in the sources opened; Lerner's Tikkun milieu is gay-affirming but Christian strands such as Wallis's are more divided.

abortion-legal.rationale: The sources never state a position and religious progressives are split on abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wallis argues faith belongs in public debate and Lerner wants spiritual values brought into politics, while opposing imposing any one religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Wallis credits faith communities with civil rights leadership; no source details remedies, so inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by any source and likely split between religious and secular strands.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from the universalist globalization of love and caring over national particularism.

gradual-change.rationale: Lerner calls for a fundamental change in the bottom line of society, not incremental reform; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the global solidarity and generosity ethic.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Lerner favors global cooperation through a Global Marshall Plan, but does not discuss the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Lerner contrasts a globalization of love and caring with the existing globalization of selfishness.

nation-first.rationale: Lerner's Global Marshall Plan has rich countries giving 1-2% of GDP annually to end global poverty, the opposite of putting national interests first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents prize both human rights and peace, and the sources only oppose Iraq and Iran strikes.

open-borders.rationale: National borders should eventually be open: Lerner's global generosity pulls toward openness, yet the sources never discuss migration and adherents divide over open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Lerner urges consuming less and rethinking what counts as progress.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Lerner says ecological sanity is central and that an ecological movement must be spiritual; no specific climate program cited.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the argument that spiritual transformation, not technique, is needed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from ecological and peace concerns.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lerner urges building a better world and a peace movement, not violent revolution; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the grassroots, values-driven approach.

central-planning.rationale: Economic democracy and love-based values are not equated with central planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Lerner's economic democracy could fit this but no source states it.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is a technical fiscal device that none of the sources mention and that the movement's ethics do not decide.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to tax cuts for the rich.

basic-income.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the anti-poverty goal.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The sources oppose selfish globalization but also global solidarity, so inference is unclear.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Lerner wants institutions steered by love and caring, but neither source says the state should pick strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Lerner's economic democracy and communal sharing point away from concentrated ownership, but the sources never endorse a distributist small-owner program.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Lerner aims to reform the bottom line by which money-making is judged, not to end money or wage labor; his reform framework implies disagreement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A market-led money regime clashes with the New Bottom Line critique of market ethics, though no source mentions central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies fixing wages are not discussed by Lerner or Wallis, and nothing in their ethics points clearly either way.

one-party-rule.rationale: The network works by persuading legislators and the public, a pluralist method that excludes a single guiding party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is never discussed; the movement's democratic progressive orientation implies mild disagreement.

democracy-best.rationale: Lerner's covenant approach lobbies elected representatives, which presumes democracy, but neither source defends it against bad voter choices.

direct-votes.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses referendums versus representation, and the movement does not take a side.

workers-councils.rationale: Economic democracy is advocated generally, but no source proposes councils as the basis of political power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not discussed and the ethic of mutual kindness gives no clear direction.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lerner's ethic of equal spiritual worth and opposition to domination rejects any natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Lerner promotes a peace movement and a Strategy of Generosity, but no source speaks of an absolute ban on political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lerner wants a Strategy of Generosity in place of domination and demands an end to the Iraq war, a view hostile to glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wallis explicitly does not seek to erase the line yet wants faith voices in debate, and Lerner opposes imposing a religion, leaving adherents on both sides of strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing one particular religion on everyone and criticizes the religious right's use of the Bible to justify policy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatizing core public functions contradicts the New Bottom Line, though this is deduced rather than stated.

military-superiority.rationale: Lerner replaces a Strategy of Domination with a Strategy of Generosity, so pursuing military superiority is rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: A nation defined by one ethnicity conflicts with the universal globalization of love and caring Lerner proposes, though he does not address it directly.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Lerner frames change as a transformation of values and consciousness rather than conflict, saying the goal is not to defeat the right but to build a better world.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Economic equality is a stated shared goal, but the sources do not say whether this means outcomes or opportunity and adherents differ.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed in opened sources; a social-justice, ecology-minded movement would likely sympathize with indigenous land claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Lerner's Global Marshall Plan transfers wealth to poor countries, but he frames it as generosity rather than reparations owed for colonialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Uniting by shared civilization sits poorly with Lerner's interfaith, global framing, but is unaddressed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Lerner names selfishness as the defect of the present system and replaces it with an ethic of caring and generosity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The caring ethic stresses obligation to others, yet the movement is also rights-supporting, so sources give no ranking.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Lerner speaks of awe at the universe and ecological sanity, and says the ecological movement must be spiritual, implying nature's worth beyond use.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is absent from the sources and spiritual progressives hold no shared line.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Lerner attacks consumerism and ecological damage but proposes rebuilding cities, not rejecting industrial society as a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: His call to rethink progress and consume less suggests suspicion of disruptive acceleration, though technology is not discussed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed anywhere in the sources and the movement is divided between caution and openness.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Institutions judged by love and caring sit uneasily with algorithmic rule, but this is deduced from his institutional ethic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is outside the sources and adherents have no shared view.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement seeks a transformed future society grounded in love and caring rather than restoring an earlier order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The New Bottom Line is a moral test applied to results, so Lerner would reject pure pragmatism that ignores ethical standards.

direct-action.rationale: Sojourners and Tikkun use protest and lobbying alike, so neither is prioritized over elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Lerner wants the anti-war movement to embody generosity and kindness, matching methods to the world he seeks.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Lerner wants eco-friendly cities and less consumption, not abandonment of civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Nothing in the sources suggests this; Lerner's reforms keep ordinary economic institutions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Lerner supports communal sharing of many produced goods and ending poverty, near a need-based principle.

production-for-use.rationale: The New Bottom Line asks that productivity be judged by love, social justice and ecological sanity rather than profit alone.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Lerner criticizes profit-maximization as a value but the sources do not adopt a theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A nonviolent, generosity-based movement is incompatible with class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organization is not covered by any source consulted.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lerner links selfishness and domination to war but never claims inevitable imperial war from capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Lerner objects to tax cuts for the rich and defends social programs funded by government.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; a caring ethic asks more than harm avoidance, yet no source discusses limits on state power over adults.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The communal sharing and caring ethic suggests rights are not only individual, but no source states it.

conscription.rationale: Deduced from the peace commitments and opposition to the Iraq war.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A movement built on political participation and lobbying values voice, deduced rather than stated.

state-as-business.rationale: The New Bottom Line rejects running institutions by profit and efficiency measures.

positive-liberty.rationale: Lerner ties universal health care and education to a higher standard of living, consistent with this view though he does not state the theory.

media-academia-power.rationale: Sources focus on money and the religious right's power rather than universities and media, so this is deduced disagreement.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Biological racial hierarchy conflicts with the equal spiritual worth of all, though unaddressed.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist-style representation is not discussed by the movement's writers.

total-state.rationale: The movement seeks a loving society through voluntary moral transformation and persuasion, not state control of all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Moral renewal is sought, but globally and without decadence rhetoric about the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansion is the Strategy of Domination that Lerner explicitly rejects.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath-based authority is absent from the sources and at odds with democratic values.

bound-labor.rationale: Serf-like obligations contradict the justice and dignity commitments, although never discussed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; adherents may sympathize with critiques of power but also affirm spiritual truths.

universal-morality.rationale: Lerner treats love and caring as values shared across religious traditions, but says nothing about reason as the route to them.

single-common-good.rationale: Wallis appeals to the common good, but sources do not say whether interests are balanced or unified.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Lerner supports a two-state solution for Israel and Palestine, which accepts Israel as a state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Lerner discusses peace between the two sides but not a general right of return.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reviving a lapsed language is a nationalist-cultural project outside the spiritual left's concerns, with no basis for a lean.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Lerner advocates economic democracy and a New Bottom Line applied to corporations.

school-vouchers.rationale: Lerner's support for adequate education for everyone suggests public provision over vouchers, but vouchers are not mentioned.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Wallis calls budgets moral documents, implying spending on the poor should not yield to deficit rules.

economic-freedom.rationale: His critique of market ethos means economic freedom as a precondition is not endorsed, though not stated.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral exemplars matter to Wallis's prophetic style, but no source says government should rely on rulers' example instead of laws.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supports two states in Israel and Palestine, but no source states a general principle of self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Lerner demands an end to the Iraq war and opposes striking Iran, from which opposition to unilateral force follows.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Lerner criticizes progressives' hostility to spiritual consciousness and seeks awe and love alongside rationality.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The globalization of love and caring suggests extending support beyond citizens, but is not spelled out.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Lerner opposes cutting social programs for the poor, so conditioning them on work is likely rejected.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lerner favors cooperation and kindness over conflict, but does not discuss employers and workers specifically.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Destroying inherited cultural institutions has no support in the sources.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc against Western powers conflicts with the Strategy of Generosity, but is unmentioned.

workers-nation.rationale: Lerner's global solidarity conflicts with organizing by nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Law fixing gender roles opposes the progressive orientation, though no source addresses it.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is a historic religious theme but no source makes it part of the modern spiritual left.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wallis credits faith communities with driving the civil rights movement, whose aim was ending legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Lerner treats government as a vehicle for loving legislation through covenant lobbying, not a pure class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Lerner's ecological emphasis conflicts with expanding fossil fuel output, though energy policy is not specified.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The movement's openness and interfaith respect suggest disagreement, but it is not stated.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the spiritual left.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is outside the sources.

national-mission.rationale: Wallis objects to the faith of Jesus being made pro-war and pro-American, rejecting national missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The opened sources never discuss gender, but a progressive movement would likely agree.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lerner criticizes money in politics but does not call politicians corrupt as a class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts the equal spiritual worth ethic though unaddressed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement's concern for justice and for victims of state violence suggests support for accountability, though no opened source discusses prosecutions of security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Lerner explicitly supports government health care, education and anti-poverty programs.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the commitment to equal worth, though not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Lerner's ethic of love and caring for all, and a globalization of generosity, rests on the equal worth of every person.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist debate the spiritual left does not engage.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Lerner urges both Israelis and Palestinians to treat each other kindly rather than apply a colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; religious pluralism and equal law pull in different directions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing a religion on everyone, which includes legally restricting free religious choice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A sectarian legal restriction unlikely to attract this movement, though not addressed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sources do not address school religion, and progressive believers divide on it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state doctrine outside the movement's concerns.

consent-of-governed.rationale: A movement relying on lobbying and democratic persuasion presupposes consent, but states no theory of legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export drives conflict with global solidarity, deduced.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority contradicts the kindness and mutual respect Lerner urges between peoples.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Strictly libertarian formulation not addressed; the movement is pacifist-leaning but supports state redistribution.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Lerner's New Bottom Line replaces selfishness and struggle with caring and cooperation as the basis of society.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; free speech and anti-extremism concerns pull in different directions.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Lerner's critique of the Strategy of Domination resonates with this view though he does not use the concept.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed in the sources.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lerner builds change through broad spiritual and democratic persuasion, not a revolutionary elite.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Wallis argues poverty is a religious issue and that budgets neglecting the poor are unbiblical.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is outside the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Lerner's pro-worker economic democracy suggests opposition to limits, though never discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Lerner attributes poverty to selfishness and unequal distribution of resources, not population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not mentioned and its fit with a values-based reform movement is unclear.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His opposition to a Strategy of Domination suggests suspicion of emergency powers, deduced.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing in scarcity is a technical question the sources do not discuss and their ethics do not settle.

party-controls-media.rationale: State control of information contradicts the democratic, persuasion-based approach.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army belongs to one-party systems the movement does not hold.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Long waits conflict with a generous global ethic, deduced.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lerner criticizes money in politics but nothing says representatives should earn only an average wage.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not a concern of this non-party spiritual movement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Global cooperation through a Global Marshall Plan suggests sympathy for pooled sovereignty, but supranational unions are not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive concentration of power runs against the movement's anti-domination stance.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the sources and varies by denomination.

clerical-rule.rationale: Lerner criticizes the religious right's political use of religion and opposes imposing a religion.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement opposes the Iraq war but does not call for defeat of its own government.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship conflicts with the movement's liberal side, though unaddressed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Concern over concentrated power and money in politics suggests mild opposition to unlimited re-election, but term rules are not discussed.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are never discussed, though participatory instincts could favor them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The sources oppose war but do not discuss permanent alliances or troop deployment.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: An extreme ownership mandate nobody in the sources proposes.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry conflicts with the peace emphasis.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nation reunification is not a theme; Lerner's only territorial position is a two-state solution for Israel and Palestine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Lerner prefers ecologically rebuilt cities and does not exalt rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not a theme of the movement, which includes many clergy and academics.

death-penalty.rationale: A compassion-centered ethic suggests opposition to executions, though the sources never discuss capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: A progressive movement likely supports it, but the sources are silent.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Lerner's progressive religion rejects the religious right's use of scripture in policy.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Religious and liberal strands of the spiritual left disagree.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-only citizenship conflicts with universalism, though unaddressed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Respect for diverse communities suggests support, but not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions pit religious liberty against equal law; the sources do not choose.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individuality is not discussed; communal spirituality and liberal tolerance point opposite ways.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Lerner's Global Marshall Plan to end poverty suggests sympathy for debt relief, though cancellation itself is not mentioned.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: An anti-colonial theme the sources do not engage.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is outside the sources and the movement has no constitutional program.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Suspending freedoms for growth contradicts a values-first democratic movement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Lerner's Global Marshall Plan has advanced countries dedicate 1-2% of GDP annually for twenty years to end poverty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The peace commitment points away from independent nuclear arsenals.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Electoral design for heads of state is not covered by the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Lerner would want economic institutions answerable to a New Bottom Line beyond price stability, but central banks go unmentioned.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Lerner's two-state solution and call for mutual kindness imply compromise over territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The New Bottom Line holds that economic activity should be judged by love, justice and ecological sanity rather than private gain alone.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An internal debate on the Marxist left that the spiritual left does not take up.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Lerner's stress on ecological sanity suggests acting early on environmental risk, though he does not state it.

collective-defense.rationale: The movement opposes wars like Iraq, but nothing in the sources addresses alliance guarantees.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed beyond Israel and Palestine two-state support.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Wallis and Lerner want faith voices in public life, so curbing religious institutions is unlikely.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Peace commitments suggest reluctance to use force, though secession is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements are not addressed by the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine rulers embody domination and misuse of religion that Lerner condemns.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Lerner opposes tax cuts for the rich, implying support for progressive rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Spiritual traditions stress both nature and nurture; unaddressed.

space-expansion.rationale: Lerner's focus on ecological sanity and caring for this world suggests space expansion is not central.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass leader worship is domination of a kind the movement rejects.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not addressed and family-law views differ among adherents.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist debate the movement does not engage.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not discussed, though anti-poverty commitments might favor it in poor countries.

refugee-return.rationale: Lerner urges kindness between sides but takes no stand on return of refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming territory by nationality conflicts with the peace stance.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing religion, including punishing departure from it.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed; global solidarity does not settle the question.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic-kin unions contradict the universalist ethos, but unaddressed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy models are not discussed by the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Lerner's Israel and Palestine positions do not address diaspora strategy of this kind.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement's premise that ethical and spiritual change drives society opposes materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Curbing concentrated corporate power fits Lerner's critique of corporate influence.

no-bailouts.rationale: Moral objection to cuts for the poor while the rich are favored suggests tolerance for bailouts is limited, but bailouts are not discussed; weak lean.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Progressive concern for minority rights suggests disagreement, though unaddressed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Progressive orientation suggests agreement but sources are silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: An autarkic bloc conflicts with Lerner's global solidarity and Marshall Plan, though autarky is not discussed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Lerner's alternative to a globalization of selfishness implies trade tied to labor and ecological standards, in line with his stated New Bottom Line.

moral-incentives.rationale: The New Bottom Line values love and generosity above the profit motive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Armed vanguard action contradicts the nonviolent Strategy of Generosity.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Egalitarian orientation implies agreement, but unaddressed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nation-centered history conflicts with the global ethos.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Paternal imperial rule is domination of the type Lerner rejects.

patriotic-education.rationale: Lerner's global ethic suggests lukewarm response to nationalist schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Wallis's racial justice concern suggests support for remedies, though preferences are not discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed by the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lerner calls for transforming capitalism's bottom line but makes no claim about crisis or collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy influence conflicts with anti-domination thinking.

delink-world-market.rationale: Global solidarity and the Marshall Plan favor integration with reform, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory of imperialism that the sources do not use, though Lerner does favor transfers from rich to poor countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Wallis honors faith-led civil rights victories, which restricted private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed by the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty validity is not discussed by the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: A democratic movement favors election, deduced.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus-style unanimity rules are not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance doctrine is not discussed; Wallis and Lerner favor nonviolent protest but the statement concerns lawful removal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty versus monarchy is a British constitutional debate absent from the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Lerner's reverence for creation suggests concern for animals, though not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed, and religious ecological thought spans vegetarian to humane-use positions.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Wallis calls on the privileged to care for the poor but Lerner prefers structural change, so strands differ.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The network exists to bring spiritual values into politics through activism and covenant lobbying.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Lerner criticizes consumer culture but sources do not claim it pacifies.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not used by the sources, though Lerner does blame a culture of selfishness.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lerner sees global inequality but does not state a dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Exclusion from office conflicts with equal-worth ethics.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist debate that the spiritual left does not engage.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: A Global Marshall Plan favors aid, so aid refusal is opposed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism conflicts with the peace emphasis.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous leadership over settler descendants is not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional founding values are not discussed, and the movement's opposition to domination is general.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism is not discussed by Wallis or Lerner.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Wallis honors abolitionists and faith-driven abolition, so a downplaying view is unlikely.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument debates are not covered, and progressive believers disagree on them.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not covered; the movement's concern for the vulnerable supports attention to disadvantage, but its gender politics are not documented.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not covered; the sources never address domestic violence policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cultural relativism about political forms is not discussed, and universal and pluralist strands both exist.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military political guardianship contradicts a peace-first stance.

paid-care-work.rationale: Valuing caring labor fits the New Bottom Line but is not specifically stated.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is a shared religious value, but no source discusses it as politics and liberal and traditional adherents differ.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service selection is not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic-industry protection is not discussed; global solidarity cuts against economic nationalism while anti-corporate views cut for it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed, and religious progressives are divided.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not discussed by the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Support for public social programs suggests preference for state pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure systems are not discussed, though communal sharing themes are sympathetic.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Fiscal oversight rules are not discussed, though Wallis treats budgets as moral documents.

single-official-language.rationale: Restricting minority languages conflicts with pluralism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restricting foreign owners conflicts with global generosity but resonates with anti-corporate views; the sources do not decide.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is a legal technicality the sources do not address.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Lerner urges people to consume less and rethink progress, treating consumerism as damaging.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Funding insurgents is a Strategy of Domination.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Troop interventions to enforce loyalty conflict with peace commitments.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lerner highlights money in politics as a core field of NSP work.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; restricting NGOs conflicts with civil society values.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Natalist policy is not discussed and the movement has no line on population decline.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local purchase limits are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Anti-poverty and economic democracy goals suggest support, but not stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed by the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Civil disobedience tradition exists but a general denial is unlikely.

non-intervention.rationale: Pacifist-leaning but also sympathetic to humanitarian concerns.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed, even if unions as such are likely welcomed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy against minorities contradicts equal worth.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Religious progressives generally value marriage as an institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparent government fits reform aims but not stated.

local-production.rationale: Lerner endorses ecological living but sources do not discuss localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist-style small-group organizing is not discussed; the network uses conferences and lobbying.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Global cooperation points against national supremacy.

religious-nation.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing a religion on everyone.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute and submission to a leading power is the hierarchy of domination Lerner proposes to replace with generosity.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Sharing resources is more in line with solidarity.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The distinction between personal and productive property is not discussed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold-war confrontation is at odds with the peace emphasis.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Delivery models for public services are not discussed, only the goal of universal provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Lerner criticizes progressives' hostility to spiritual life ("religio-phobia") and insists the ecological movement must be spiritual.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Lerner offers no verdict on capitalism's historical role beyond its present failure to value love and caring.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Lerner demands a transformed economic bottom line for all and a progressive gender stance is likely, but gender is not covered in opened sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of childcare and housework is not discussed.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty obligations are not discussed by the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Lerner endorses communal sharing but not a reorganization into small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement against minorities conflicts with justice commitments.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Lerner's New Bottom Line may be third-way but sources do not state it that way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Lerner supports two states and mutual respect, not primacy of one claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial contradicts truthfulness, though not addressed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing a religion on everyone.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Exploitation of colonies is domination Lerner rejects.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic juristic doctrine the Judeo-Christian spiritual left sources do not address.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Armed removal of rulers conflicts with peace commitments.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy suggests sympathy for participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A progressive movement likely agrees but not documented.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Likely support from the progressive wing but not documented.

assisted-dying.rationale: Religious progressives are divided on assisted dying and the sources are silent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Wallis claims to transcend left and right, but Lerner explicitly identifies as progressive.

alienated-labor.rationale: Lerner says modern workplaces push people to neglect meaning and love, which resembles alienation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Lerner's democratic stance implies authority from people, though unaddressed.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Likely opposes strict bans, deduced from respect for religion.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A progressive movement concerned with power and dignity would likely back it, but no opened source addresses it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Lerner's reform vision resembles a social market, though not stated.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pacifist-leaning but not stated; strands differ.

rich-first.rationale: Lerner's Marshall Plan demands solidarity rather than allowing some to prosper first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc neutrality is not discussed; the movement opposes war but not alliances as such.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit reform is not discussed by the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-poverty commitment suggests opposition to austerity conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Wealth qualification conflicts with equal worth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist themes fit the movement but are not documented.

reification.rationale: Marxist reification theory is not used by Lerner, even though his critique of treating people as means to profit is related.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Concern over money in politics suggests agreement.

racial-franchise.rationale: Wallis credits faith-driven civil rights and suffrage struggles.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency in government is not discussed by the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Lerner's interfaith network and rejection of imposing a religion contradict legal bars on mixed-faith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Singling out a religious minority for avoidance contradicts the equal worth and interfaith respect the network stands on.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concern over money in politics suggests agreement.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not covered; the sources never discuss gays in the military and Christian strands are divided.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Lerner complains that progressives suffer from religio-phobia and hostility to spiritual consciousness, so state atheism would be anathema.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolition is far from the movement's reform-oriented, legislature-lobbying program, though it is not discussed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not discussed beyond Lerner's two-state position.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Lerner opposes cutting social programs and wants government action on poverty.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk as a policy priority is not discussed, although ecological and peace concerns relate.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not stated in opened sources, but liberal religious movements such as Tikkun's milieu typically open all offices to women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not stated in opened sources; a progressive religious orientation favors equal spouses, though conservative believers differ.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights of non-citizens are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not discussed, even if the movement favors protection of the poor.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements train for national service in a way that conflicts with the peace commitment.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not discussed though the peace commitment suggests sympathy.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not discussed, though the movement opposes militarism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal recognition of genocides is not discussed in opened sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The movement criticizes profit-first values but does not distinguish work income from property income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strands split between pacifists and just-war thinkers.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sex as a social construct is not discussed and religious strands generally resist it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Academic feminist theory is not engaged by the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Glorifying death for the nation sits badly with Lerner's rejection of militarism, though martyrdom language exists in religion.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wikipedia defines the spiritual left as grounding politics in spiritual traditions, though not as a good-versus-evil struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Cultural Zionism-style ideas are not discussed beyond Lerner's two-state position.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural renewal before statebuilding is not discussed, though the movement does emphasize cultural change.

god-not-male.rationale: Progressive religion typically embraces inclusive God-language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist biblical criticism is plausible for the Tikkun milieu but not documented in opened sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reserving economic life for a majority group contradicts equal worth and the interfaith universalism of the network.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative merging of ethnic regions is not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from the state is not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definitional debate that the spiritual left does not enter.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Lerner favors universal health care and basic goods for all, which suggests public provision of essentials like hospitals and water.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal socialism is not discussed in opened sources.

family-wage.rationale: Family wage policy is not discussed, though its premise of a male breadwinner conflicts with progressive gender views.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation speed is not discussed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is not discussed and spiritual traditions are ambivalent about it.

person-over-state.rationale: A love-and-caring ethic holds each person's dignity above institutional goals, but the sources do not state the principle in this form.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wikipedia defines the position as grounding left aims in spiritual traditions, and Lerner says institutions should serve love, awe and meaning.

gm-crops.rationale: Not discussed; ecological and anti-corporate concerns suggest suspicion while sustainability goals could support it.

dense-cities.rationale: Lerner favors rebuilt, eco-friendly cities that prioritize walking over cars.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The universalist ethic and Wallis's coalition approach cut against organizing by racial interest, though Wallis does prioritize racial justice.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed; Wallis's racial-justice commitments sit alongside universalism, leaving no clear answer.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Lerner opposes the Iraq war as a war of choice, so he likely holds that force is for defense, but he does not state a general rule.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates conflict with common community.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Paranoid nationalism is not part of the movement.

free-public-college.rationale: Lerner supports adequate education for everyone as part of a higher standard of living, though tuition is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Lerner's emphasis on ecological sanity and consuming less implies support for making polluters pay, but he names no tax.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological sanity is one of the stated components of Lerner's New Bottom Line, which implies stewardship for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement stresses care and nonviolence, but the sources do not attribute them to women specifically.

arms-reduction.rationale: Lerner wants a peace movement and to redirect resources from the military to ending poverty.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital controls are not discussed, though a critique of unregulated globalization is stated.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Monopoly on arms is not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Conscientious refusal is plausible for peace-church strands but not documented for the broader spiritual left.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Global Marshall Plan restructures world economic flows toward the poor.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The network works through lobbying legislators and a covenant, which assumes the existing state can be used.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntary economic pluralism is not discussed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not discussed, and spiritual views of nature may oppose commodifying it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sacralizing the nation conflicts with universal ethics.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The anti-poverty orientation suggests sympathy, though debt relief is not discussed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation theory is not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Spiritual traditions affirm shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Concern over money in politics suggests support.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Lerner's interfaith approach seeks common values but does not claim one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural price policy is not discussed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The peace emphasis suggests opposition to keeping arsenals, but nuclear weapons are not discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: A labor party is not discussed; the network is non-partisan and works with Democrats.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed in opened sources, though human dignity commitments would likely oppose it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal legal standing of women is likely supported by a progressive religious movement, though not discussed in opened sources.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Priority rules between environment and liberty are not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A compassionate, rehabilitative ethic suggests discomfort with fixed sentences, but sentencing is not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Pro-worker economic democracy suggests opposition to right-to-work rules, but the sources do not discuss them.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing one particular religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Procedural definitions of democracy are not discussed.

premarital-sex.rationale: Strands split between liberal and traditional religious.

women-suffrage.rationale: Wallis credits faith communities with women's suffrage.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Spiritual left defends religion's positive role.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed in opened sources and adherents have no stated line.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Lerner's communal sharing of goods conflicts with first-claim property but the question is not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: International courts are not discussed, though a peace emphasis suggests sympathy.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Lerner criticizes the religious right's misuse of the Bible.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Guarantees for women within Indigenous self-government are not discussed in the opened sources, so no lean is documented.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending bureaucratic planned economies is not part of the movement's concerns, which lean toward democratic reform.

indirect-election.rationale: The participatory, grassroots orientation suggests preference for direct choice, though election design is not discussed.

national-church-status.rationale: Lerner opposes imposing one religion and the network is interfaith, so legal privilege for one church is opposed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Plebiscites on disputed land are not discussed beyond Lerner's two-state aim.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Postcolonial border doctrine is not discussed.

simple-living.rationale: Lerner urges consuming less and rethinking progress.

equal-conscription.rationale: Draft policy for women is not discussed, though pacifist strands oppose any draft.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Not discussed as a political idea, though spiritual attachment to land is a theme in Jewish thought for Lerner.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Killing suspected drug users without trial contradicts the love-and-caring ethic and basic justice.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Kin-state protection claims are not discussed but are nationalist in orientation, unlike Lerner's universal framing.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Lerner's support for communal sharing of produced goods suggests sympathy with common claims on resources, though land and Georgist ideas are not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Libertarian self-ownership is not discussed and communal ethics qualify it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Lerner supports universal health care and education.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The network itself is an interest group that lobbies and organizes, so bypassing groups contradicts its method.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Money in politics concern suggests agreement.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Denominational politics is not discussed, though the network is explicitly interfaith.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not discussed; spiritual traditions combine modernity with traditional values in varied ways.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Equal standing of spouses is likely supported by progressive believers, but the sources are silent.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource sovereignty is not discussed, though Lerner favors transfers from rich to poor nations.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Interfaith respect and equal worth conflict with this.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not stated directly, but an interfaith universalism that respects all traditions points toward cultural equality.

women-must-cover.rationale: Coerced dress conflicts with the movement's commitments.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Interfaith respect rejects claims of incompatibility.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Tort-based environmental law is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the New Bottom Line and poverty-first stance that justice in distribution is judged by care for all, not only by how wealth was acquired.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not stated; inferred from Lerner's Global Marshall Plan and critique of unregulated globalization that a small tax on financial transactions fits the programme.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not directly sourced; inferred from the movement's emphasis on justice for the poor and marginalized, which treats racism as a continuing obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not directly sourced; inferred from the prophetic tradition and the civil-rights legacy that Wallis and Lerner invoke, which holds conscience above unjust law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not stated; inferred from Lerner's call to consume less and measure the economy by meaning and care rather than output, which welcomes shorter working time.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favours global cooperation and opposes empire, which cuts both ways on separate centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Never addressed by Lerner or Wallis; adherents are not committed to Marxian value theory, so inferred as neutral.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred; Wallis and Lerner seek a patriotism of generosity and care for ordinary people, though they criticise nationalism, so the fit is partial.

material-over-identity.rationale: Lerner's politics of meaning faults the left for focusing on material interests while ignoring spiritual and ethical needs; the New Bottom Line puts love and caring above material measures.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic method and nonviolence; a communist-party-led system is outside the current and opposed to it.

missingStatements.text: Economic and public institutions should be judged by how much they promote love, caring and generosity, not only by profit and efficiency.
missingStatements.rationale: Lerner's New Bottom Line is the movement's central programmatic demand for economy, schools and government.

notes: Lerner (Jewish, explicitly progressive) and Wallis (evangelical, claims to transcend left and right) differ on abortion, same-sex marriage and church-state; those answers are held at neutral or low confidence. Most policy answers beyond economics, peace and ecology are inferences from the shared ethic.
